title: Stravinsky: The Rite of Spring
welcome_lead: 29 May 1913 — the riot at the Théâtre des Champs-Élysées.
meta_desc: A-Level Music: Stravinsky and The Rite of Spring 1913.
final_note: Rhythm seized the future of music.

concepts.def: Two or more keys sounding simultaneously.
Two or more rhythms sounding simultaneously.
Triad of two stacked major thirds.

walkthroughs.body_html: On 29 May 1913, the premiere of The Rite of Spring at the Théâtre des Champs-Élysées caused a near-riot. Nijinsky's choreography and Stravinsky's dissonance, polymetre and ostinati shocked the audience.
Stravinsky stacks rhythms (3 against 2, irregular metres) and harmonies (the famous bitonal chord at the opening of Augurs of Spring combines E-flat major and F-flat major triads).
The Rite reshaped 20th-century music — rhythm and timbre took precedence over melody. Boulez, Bernstein and minimalists all acknowledged its debt.
